Vitamins and Minerals
Vitamins and minerals from foods are made available as mac-
ronutrients and are digested and absorbed across the mucosal 
layer, primarily in the small intestine (Figure 1-9). Besides 
adequate passive and transporter mechanisms, various factors 
affect the bioavailability of vitamins and minerals, including 
the presence or absence of other specific nutrients, acid or al-
kali, phytates, and oxalates. The liters of fluid that are secreted 
each day from the GIT serve as a solvent, a vehicle for chemical 
reactions, and a medium for transfer of several nutrients.
